# Security Checklist: ISK-0003 — Configuration Schema & Validation Foundation

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for secret handling, value disclosure, hostile documents, fail-safe environments, and section isolation are complete, clear, and consistent
**Created**: 2026-11-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Value Disclosure

- [x] CHK001 - Is every output channel that must never hold a configuration value named (errors, renderings, log events, exception messages, diagnostics)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020, Contract §Field errors rule 3]
- [x] CHK002 - Is the line between a value, which is never echoed, and a key or path segment, which is echoed in a path, drawn clearly, including for undeclared keys? [Clarity, Spec §US1 scenario 1, §FR-019]
  - Keys are not values: US1 scenario 1 echoes an undeclared key in its path, and the contract builds text from the code, path, schema, and layer only.
- [x] CHK003 - Is the canary requirement measurable: which values carry the canary, which channels are searched, and that environment variable values are included? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, Tasks T024]
- [x] CHK004 - Is it specified that a revision cannot reveal a secret value? [Completeness, Spec §TR-8, Contract §Secret reference placeholders rule 8]

## Secret References

- [x] CHK005 - Is the reference name grammar fully specified, including length, character set, segment rules, and traversal? [Clarity, Spec §TR-7]
- [x] CHK006 - Is the placeholder form unambiguous against an ordinary `object` field that declares a child field named `secretRef`? [Ambiguity, Spec §TR-7, Contract §Root and namespaces rule 3]
  - Fixed: a schema could declare an `object` field with a child named `secretRef`, whose value would then look like a placeholder. The contract, research R7, and T010 now reserve the name `secretRef`, in any case, as `config.schema.invalid`.
- [x] CHK007 - Is it specified how a secret field is set from an environment variable without a pasted key being taken as a reference name, and what a `__SECRETREF` segment on a non-secret field means? [Completeness, Research R6, Contract §Environment variables rule 4]
  - Fixed: a `__SECRETREF` segment on a non-secret field had no stated outcome. The contract, research R6, and T027 now make it `config.field.type_mismatch`, as a placeholder in a document is.
- [x] CHK008 - Are the known limits of declaration-based secret detection documented? [Assumption, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §Known limits]

## Hostile Documents

- [x] CHK009 - Are the banned YAML constructs enumerated, with rejection required before any expansion? [Completeness, Spec §TR-3, §FR-011]
- [x] CHK010 - Are the size, depth, node, and string limits quantified, with the point where reading stops? [Clarity, Spec §TR-12, Contract §Limits]
- [x] CHK011 - Is the alias bomb allocation bound measurable, with an independent check that allocation does not grow with expansion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK012 - Is control-character rejection specified for decoded text (JSON `\u0000`, YAML `"\x00"`) as well as for raw bytes? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §Inputs rule 5, Research R4]
  - Fixed: research R4 checked control characters only in raw bytes, but escapes such as JSON `"\u0000"` produce them after decoding, and the spec's edge case is about strings. The contract, R4, T013, and T019 now apply the check to decoded keys and strings as well.
- [x] CHK013 - Is it specified that environment variable text faces the same control-character and string-length rules as document strings? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015]
  - Fixed: FR-015 says a variable's text has "the same errors as a document value", but nothing applied the control-character and string-length rules to it. The contract, research R6, and T027 now do, with `config.document.malformed` and `config.document.too_large`.
- [ ] CHK014 - Is it specified whether the document-level rules (well-formedness, UTF-8, limits, banned constructs, duplicate keys) apply to content outside the `iskender` root, consistently with FR-005's "never read, validated, or reported"? [Conflict, Spec §FR-005, §FR-011]
  - Open: needs a maintainer decision. See the stage's blocked result.

## Fail-Safe Environment

- [x] CHK015 - Is production-grade behavior specified for a missing environment name and for any name other than `development`? [Completeness, Spec §TR-6, §FR-016]
- [x] CHK016 - Is a field that is both required and development-only addressed, given that no value could ever validate outside `development`? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-008, §FR-016]
  - Fixed: a required, development-only field could never validate outside `development`. The contract, research R7, and T010 now make it `config.schema.invalid`.
- [x] CHK017 - Are environment variable name comparisons specified as culture-independent, so that `ISKENDER__` matches the same way under every culture (such as `tr-TR`)? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §TR-5]
  - Fixed: "without regard to case" was unqualified, and a culture-aware comparison under `tr-TR` does not match `iskender__` to `ISKENDER__`. The contract, research R6, and T027 now require ordinal comparison that folds only ASCII letters.

## Isolation and Integrity

- [x] CHK018 - Is section isolation specified so that one module cannot read another's section, with the in-process limit stated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, Contract §Known limits]
- [x] CHK019 - Is the ban on partly valid configurations specified for every failure path, including document errors? [Coverage, Spec §FR-022, Contract §Snapshot rule 1]
- [x] CHK020 - Is the operator-only scope, with no tenant impersonation, stated? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions, Contract §Root and namespaces rule 6]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
